Subject: VenueAI: 90-day token profile and model options

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for the kickoff this morning. Per our discussion, attaching the spreadsheet with the 90-day hourly token profile you filled out during the call and the three sample context files you shared. I also attached our initial model shortlist (redwood_model_shortlist-v1.pdf) with quick notes on tradeoffs.

Goals for this thread:
- Confirm peak-hour tokens and tail characteristics we should optimize for (latency vs cost).
- Agree on context-window needs (short chat vs long document extraction).
- Pick 2 candidate model variants for the PoC (one latency-optimized, one cost-optimized).

Quick asks for you: could you confirm the following by EOD Wednesday?
1) Average and 95th percentile tokens per user event (you provided daily totals; we need per-event breakdown).
2) Typical context length for the longest request (examples attached in venueai_poc_context_samples.txt).
3) Any regulatory constraints about data retention or in-region processing (EU vs US).

What you can expect from us this week: Grace will circulate a short-sizing note with recommended batch sizes, an initial throughput estimate, and a fallback plan if the long-context variant increases latency beyond your SLOs. Ben will prepare a quick cost delta comparing FP16 vs 4-bit quantized variants for predicted monthly token volumes. I will coordinate the integration playbook.

Attachments: venueai_prod_token_profile.xlsx (your upload, anonymized), venueai_poc_context_samples.txt, redwood_model_shortlist-v1.pdf

Thanks —

From: Elena Park <elena@venueai.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VenueAI: 90-day token profile and model options

Monica — thanks for the summary and the files. Quick answers below and a couple clarifications inline.

1) Per-event breakdown (approx):
- Short query (autosuggest / one-line summary): median ~30 tokens, 95th ~120 tokens.
- Multi-field extraction (5-8 fields from receipts): median ~250 tokens, 95th ~1,100 tokens.
- Long doc summarization (single-doc up to ~4k words): median ~5,000 tokens, 95th ~9,800 tokens (rare, ~2% of calls).

2) Longest requests: our nightly batch jobs (PDF ingestion + question answering) are the long ones — often 8k-10k token context across multiple documents. For the PoC, we plan to route those to an offline workflow and keep real-time API calls to <=2k tokens, but we want the option to fall back to an online long-context model for high-priority customers.

3) Data residency: production must stay in-us for now (no EU processing). We will share SOC 2 reports if required during contract review.

Notes on traffic shape: peak concurrent active users in month 1 expected ~850, with a daily average of ~35k user events. Peak hours concentrated 14:00-16:00 PT (approx 25% of daily traffic).

Happy to hop on a short call if you need to walk through the attached samples.

—Elena
Elena Park
Head of Product, VenueAI
elena@venueai.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@venueai.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VenueAI: 90-day token profile and model options

Folks — reading Elena's numbers, I'm proposing the following concise model shortlist and an initial sizing rationale:

Candidate A — "rwd-lowlatency-3B" (latency-optimized)- Best for RT paths (autosuggest / short query). Strong 99th percentile latency at 2k seq, minimal KV cache overhead. Estimated qps per GPU: ~220 (2k token window, batch=8, 16g cache).

Candidate B — "rwd-cost-13B-q4" (cost-optimized, quantized)- Suited for multi-field extraction and mid-length summaries (up to 2k online). Q4 quantization reduces GPU memory and per-token cost by ~35% vs FP16. Estimated qps per GPU: ~65 (2k token window, batch=4).

Candidate C — "rwd-long-32B" (long-context experimental)- Provides a 8k+ context path, but expect latency penalties for hot online traffic. Recommend offline routing for 8k+ jobs (as Elena suggested) and reserve C for canary/paid-tier fallbacks.

Sizing notes (rough initial):
- Target PoC configuration: 2x lowlatency (A) GPUs for RT tier, 1x cost-optimized (B) GPU pool for bursty mid-length calls, and a single reserved slot for C in a cold-standby to run canary long-context fallbacks.
- Based on Elena's peak-hour distribution and token mix, this setup covers ~95% of expected realtime requests with headroom for 20% peak burst (autoscaling + burst capacity).

Immediate asks from product/ops:
- Ben, can you run a cost delta for 50M vs 200M monthly tokens on A vs B? Include quantized vs FP16 numbers.
- Marcus, please draft a simple routing policy for: short (<200 tokens) => A, mid (200-2k) => B, long (>2k) => offline/C fallback.

I will draft a short runbook describing how we instrument prefix caching for receipts extraction to cut duplicated tokens in half.

Grace O'Connor
Head, Customer Success Engineering | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

- Marcus: routing policy draft + example Rego snippet for canary -> due Fri COB.

2) Customer deliverables:

- Elena: confirm per-event breakdown if any of the mid-length events are likely to spike >2k tokens in 10%+ of calls (we need to know whether to size B for occasional 3-4k tail).

- 2x rwd-lowlatency-3B (RT)
- 1x rwd-cost-13B-q4 (mid)
- 1x reserved cold-standby rwd-long-32B for canary fallbacks
